# Draft:Pamina Stewart

----
Pamina Stewart (born 1960s) is a British sculptor and environmental artist known for creating animal sculptures from recycled and organic materials. Based in Birmingham, England, Stewart has exhibited internationally and held artist residencies in Canada, Finland, and the Czech Republic. Her work explores the relationship between humans, animals, and environmental sustainability through the transformation of discarded materials.
Early life and education
Stewart studied art in the West Midlands, earning a Foundation in Art from Lanchester Polytechnic (1984–85), followed by a BA (Hons) Fine Art First Class from Stourbridge College of Art (1986–89). She completed an MA Fine Art at Birmingham Institute of Art and Design (1989–90). Later, she earned a BSc (Hons) Psychology from The Open University (1991–95) and an MA in Video Games Development from Birmingham City University (2013–14).
Artistic practice
Stewart's sculptural practice centers on environmental themes, transforming discarded materials into animal forms that explore human-nature relationships. She combines traditional sculptural techniques with crafting, sewing, painting and printing. Her materials include discarded modern items such as obsolete technology and food packaging, alongside renewable resources.
The Plastific Ocean
A significant ongoing body of work, "The Plastific Ocean" series focuses on ocean plastic pollution. Stewart creates sculptures of sea creatures using waste plastic. Each sculpture is made entirely from intercepted waste that would otherwise end up in the ocean, including plastic boxes, caps, bottles, netting, textiles, string, wool, snack packs and socks. The series aims to raise awareness about reducing plastic waste and its environmental impact on marine life.
Career
Early career (1990s)
Stewart began exhibiting in 1990 with a solo exhibition "Paintings and Prints" at Malvern Workshop, Worcestershire. In the mid-1990s, she participated in international residencies including Gallery 101 in Ottawa, Canada (1995) and Young Artists Gallery in Prague, Czech Republic (1994).
During this period, Stewart was awarded several grants from West Midlands Arts, including Project Funding Support (1993), New Work and Productions Award (1996), and New Work and Commissions Award (1999).
Museum recognition (2000s)
Stewart's work gained institutional recognition with inclusion in "Art of Birmingham II 1939–2008" at Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery in 2008. She held a solo exhibition "Phobia: Robots" at Midland Arts Centre, Birmingham in 2002. During this period, she completed major public commissions including the Birmingham Bull (2008), a twice life-sized sculpture made from recycled cans, commissioned by Coca-Cola for recycling week.
Stewart continued to receive Arts Council England funding during this period, including Arts Awards in 2006 and 2008.
Gallery representation (2010s)
From 2009–2017, Stewart was represented by Rebecca Hossack Gallery in London, a gallery that was the first in Europe to exhibit Australian Aboriginal art. She participated in multiple art fairs including London Art Fair, New York Art Fair, and Toronto. Her work was exhibited at the gallery's Charlotte Street location and Mott Street, New York venue. She participated in "Dark Matter" at Rebecca Hossack Gallery, New York in 2017.
Recent work (2020s)
Recent exhibitions include "Island Nations" at Joshibi Museum and Art Gallery, Tokyo (2021) and "Ikon for Artists" at Ikon Gallery, Birmingham (2021). The Ikon Gallery exhibition featured over 250 Birmingham artists in a response to COVID-19's impact on artists' incomes.
In 2018, Stewart participated in "Coventry Open" at Herbert Art Gallery and Museum, Coventry, a competitive biennial exhibition where 99 works were selected from 330 submissions by a professional jury.
Recent exhibitions (2022-2025) include "Look Closely" at Stirchley Happenings Art Trail (2022), "Art in Mind" at The Bricklane Gallery, London (2022), "Climate Matters" at The Bridge Gallery, Tynemouth (2023), and "Sustainability in Practice" at John Moores University (2024).
Public commissions
Stewart has completed several significant public art commissions:
* Birmingham Bull (2008): Twice life-sized bull sculpture made from recycled cans, commissioned by Coca-Cola for recycling week
* Pony Trail (2010): Life-size pit pony sculpture in Brierley Hill, West Midlands, duplicated 30 times and decorated by other artists for a public art trail
* Weathervane (2003): Commissioned for Centro Information Points, Birmingham
Installations and site-specific works
Stewart has created numerous installations and site-specific works, often responding to local themes and using locally sourced materials.
Propagated2021
During the COVID-19 pandemic, Stewart organized "Propagated2021," a project ensuring artists could continue to create and exhibit work safely during lockdown. Each participating artist designed individual artworks and shared construction instructions digitally. Stewart's contribution was a series of "Forest Guardians" - creatures including owls, badgers, and hares made from hard-to-recycle food packaging and renewable natural materials, designed to watch over and protect Moseley Park.
French Open Gardens Programme
Stewart participated annually in France's Open Gardens programme, funded by the Ministry of Culture (France), creating site-specific works at Cairnhill in Rioux-Martin. These included "The Willowmen" (2015), "The Knitted Conkers" (2016), willow hens for "Animals in the Garden," and crickets for "Sounds of the Garden," all made using locally sourced materials.
Finland installations
During her residencies in Finland, Stewart created "The Neighbours" (2001), a 12 × 9 metre installation depicting two knitted bears sourced from a charity shop in Lahti, as part of the city-wide arts trail "!hah!".
Artist residencies
* Gallery 101, Ottawa, Canada (1995)
* Young Artists Gallery, Prague, Czech Republic (1994)
* Lahti Art Association, Finland (1999)
* Cannon Hill Nature Reserve, Birmingham (1996)
Awards and funding
Stewart has received sustained support from Arts Council England spanning three decades:
* Arts Council Lottery Funding Project Grant (2020)
* Arts Award, Arts Council West Midlands (2008)
* Creative Workspace Grant, Birmingham City Council (2008)
* Arts Awards, Arts Council West Midlands (2006)
* Feasibility Funding, Birmingham City Council (2005)
* Creative Ambition Award, West Midlands Arts (2000)
* New Work and Commissions Award, West Midlands Arts (1999)
* New Work and Productions Award, West Midlands Arts (1996)
* Project Funding Support Award, West Midlands Arts (1993)
* 'Go and See' Grant, The Prince's Trust (1991)
* Nancie Cleve Award (1989)
